data.narrative:
Axiom Space, a Series G space infrastructure company founded by Michael T. Suffredini and Kam Ghaffarian, has raised $350M to date. The Space & Aerospace sector contains 6 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX and Rocket Lab, though narrow-filter peer matching proved insufficient for reliable median-based valuation.

Stage-progression analysis was the sole applicable triangulation method. Using $175M (derived from total capital raised as a proxy for implied post-Series F valuation) and applying a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G advancement, this method yields an implied valuation of $219M. Public-comp anchoring, while informed by a Space & Aerospace P/S median of 25.3x across the sector, cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue. Peer-median triangulation was skipped due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private comparables meeting statistical thresholds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $186M to $252M, centered on $219M. This range is derived mechanically from stage-progression methodology and represents considerable uncertainty. Key risks include reliance on a single applicable method, lack of revenue disclosure for cross-check anchoring, and limited homogeneous private peer data at Series G in frontier aerospace. The true valuation likely reflects undisclosed customer contracts and development milestones not captured in this analysis.
